sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Constitutional Basis**: Freedom of the press is not explicitly mentioned but is implied under **Article 19(1)(a)** (Freedom of Speech and Expression) as interpreted by the Supreme Court in *Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras*.
• **Reasonable Restrictions**: Under **Article 19(2)**, the state can impose restrictions on grounds of sovereignty, integrity, security of the state, public order, decency, or morality.
• **Institutional Oversight**: The **Press Council of India (PCI)**, established under the Press Council Act, 1978, acts as a quasi-judicial body to maintain professional standards.
• **Key Metric**: The transition from 'Missionary Journalism' (pre-1947) to 'Commercial/Corporate Journalism' (post-1990s liberalization).

items.definition: A statutory, quasi-judicial body that acts as a watchdog. It has no punitive powers to punish editors/journalists but can 'censure' them.
Established under the Prasar Bharati Act, 1990, it is an autonomous body comprising All India Radio and Doordarshan to ensure public service broadcasting.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Emergency Era (1975-77)**: Pre-censorship imposed; led to the formation of the Editors Guild of India.
• **Digital Media Rules (2021)**: IT Rules under the IT Act, 2000, bringing digital news portals under regulatory oversight.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Paid news, cross-media ownership, fake news, and 'Trial by Media'.
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the PCI, self-regulation, and transparency in ownership disclosure.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'R-M-P' (Rajadhyaksha-Mathew-PCI).
• **Decoded Meaning**: 1st Commission (Rajadhyaksha), 2nd Commission (Mathew), Resulting in the Press Council of India.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: The Press Council of India has NO power to punish or fine journalists; it can only 'censure' or 'admonish'. Do not confuse it with a court of law.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Democratic Accountability' and 'Fourth Estate' when discussing the role of the press in holding the executive accountable.

keyTakeaways: Freedom of press is a derivative right under Article 19(1)(a).
The Press Council of India is a statutory body, not a constitutional one.
Post-1990s, the shift from state-controlled media to corporate-dominated media has created new challenges regarding 'Paid News' and 'Media Trials'.
